anomalies.obs: On the Power sheet, the +12V arrow feeds a junction dot that ties BOTH pin 1 and pin 2 of J7 and of J8 to +12V. J8 pin 4 is the only ground return on either header; J7 pin 4 is left as a no-connect (X), so J7 has no ground path at all. A standard 4-pin fan header uses pin 1 = GND, pin 2 = +12V, pin 3 = tach, pin 4 = PWM.
anomalies.exp: Per the specification the +12V rail includes only 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)'; pin 1 must not be on +12V. Sound practice (and the spec's statement that the board 'monitors 2 fan tachometers ... and raises a run fault if a fan stalls') requires each header to supply +12V on pin 2 and a ground return (pin 1), so the fans can actually spin.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (page 7): J7 pins 1 and 2 both wired to the +12V junction dot, pin 3 -> FAN_0_TACH, pin 4 -> no-connect (X); J8 pins 1 and 2 both to +12V, pin 3 -> FAN_1_TACH, pin 4 -> GND.
Also on this net [+12V]: ... the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2).

anomalies.impact: The fan ground pin is shorted to +12V on both headers, and J7 has no return path whatsoever, so neither fan receives the correct 12 V-to-GND supply; the fans will not run, the tach inputs will read a constant stall condition, and the firmware's fan-fault logic / actual oven airflow will be wrong (and a plugged-in fan could be damaged by having its ground pin driven to +12V).

parsed.summary: The MCU, thermocouple, power-mux, buck and heater-switch sections all match the specification, but the two fan headers appear miswired: pin 1 of J7 and J8 is tied to +12V (the spec lists only pin 2 on that rail) and J7 has no ground return at all, so the fans cannot be powered as intended.
